subject.title: Feature: configurable bootstrap file injection order for prompt cache optimization

question: Should OpenClaw add core configuration for bootstrap file volatility/order, and should that be exact filenames, full order control, or a broader context-volatility API?
rationale: The source-proven gap is real, but the requested solution adds new config/default surface in a central prompt-cache path where repository policy requires maintainer product intent before implementation.

options.title: Design one core volatility/order config
options.body: Add a single documented config contract covering dynamic/cache-boundary placement and ordering, with stable defaults and focused tests for current and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Extend plugin/context hooks instead
options.body: Keep core config smaller by exposing enough plugin or context-engine metadata for deployments to classify volatile bootstrap context outside core defaults.

options.title: Decline the new knob
options.body: Document the current supported mitigations such as contextInjection and workspace-file discipline, leaving arbitrary file volatility/order control out of core for now.

recommendation.title: Design one core volatility/order config
recommendation.body: Add a single documented config contract covering dynamic/cache-boundary placement and ordering, with stable defaults and focused tests for current and upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent authored the current cache-ordering and contextInjection history around this path, so they are the strongest routing candidate for the API shape decision.
